Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships for CT Students 2024 is an opportunity offered by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) of Japan to Indian undergraduate students. Applicants are required to choose a specific field of study from the below-given options that include -
The scholarship program will begin in April 2024 and end in March 2028. Selected students will receive a monthly allowance of 117,000 yen (approximately INR 71,200) and other benefits.
To be eligible, an applicant must -
have born on or after 2nd April 1999
have scored a minimum of 65% in Class 11/12
have completed 11 years of schooling in countries other than Japan
be willing to learn the Japanese language
arrive in Japan between 1st April 2024-7th April 2024
have a newly issued student visa
Preference will be given to candidates who are proficient in the Japanese language.
Applicants who will meet the above conditions by March 2024 are eligible to apply.
Candidates who are military personnel or military civilian employees at the time of their arrival in Japan or during the payment of the scholarship are not eligible.
Students who have already received MEXT scholarships are not eligible.
Candidates who cannot arrive in Japan by the last date of joining the host institution are not eligible.
Candidates who are enrolled in other programs under the Japanese Government (MEXT) are not eligible.
Students who already have a ‘student’ visa for Japan and are enrolled in any institution/university in Japan are not eligible.
Candidates who are planning to apply/have received scholarships from any other organisation in Japan are not eligible.
For more information, kindly refer to the ‘Scholarship Guidelines’ document.
Selected candidates will be provided with the following benefits -

Selected candidates will receive 11,7000 yen (approximately INR 71,200) each month. They will also receive a supplemental regional allowance of up to 3,000 yen per month to study and conduct research in specially designated regions.
All the fees related to entrance examinations, matriculation, and tuition at colleges of technology will be covered by the Government of Japan (MEXT).
Transportation to Japan will be stipulated by the Government of Japan (MEXT). Flight tickets for an economy class will be provided to students to visit the designated institutions.
Note - For more information, kindly refer to the ‘Scholarship Guidelines’ document.

A list of the addresses is listed below -
Consulate General of Japan in Kolkata
(for students residing in West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar and Odisha)
Consulate General of Japan in Chennai
(for students residing in Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana)
Japan Information Centre, Embassy of Japan,
(for students in the remaining states and union territories)
All the applications need to be sent by post or courier. The envelope must have ‘Application for CoT Scholarship 2024’ marked on it.
No applications will be accepted through emails.
The Japanese diplomatic missions will conduct the first screening of applicants by reviewing the submitted application documents, written academic examinations and interviews.
A maximum of 12 scholarships will be awarded.
During the written examination for selection, candidates cannot use calculators or other devices.
If a candidate makes a false statement on the application then the scholarship will not be provided.
In case of violating the articles of the pledge to the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology, candidates will not receive the scholarship.
If a candidate violates any Japanese laws and is sentenced/imprisoned for an indefinite period or a period exceeding 1 year will be ineligible for the scholarship.
Candidates receiving constant poor grades in their academics and having no scope for improvement will become ineligible for the scholarship.
Candidates receiving any other scholarship during their study in Japan will not be eligible to continue to be a grantee of the scholarship.
In case of unforeseen or unavoidable circumstances, the Japanese Government reserves the right to change or cancel the arrival date, scholarship, and contents of the application guidelines.
